summary: Chat streaming kickoff delays observed after inference stack upgrade (model + runtime)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Greenfield AI reported that chat sessions started failing to emit the first streamed token for multiple requests after we deployed the runtime 2.1.6 + model bundle update to the dedicated pool in us-east-1 on 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.

Impact:
- Several customers on the dedicated cluster experienced elevated TTFB for chat completions (affecting interactive product demos).
- p50 first-token latency increased from ~80ms to ~420ms; p95/p99 increases observed and occasional streaming timeouts at the client layer.
- Customer-visible: long pauses before the first token, then normal token cadence. No consistent 5xx returns observed.

Environment / Scope:
- Affected: dedicated capacity pool greenfield-dedicated-1 in us-east-1.
- Runtime version rolled to 2.1.6 at 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC; model bundles updated to redwood/gpt-medium-v1@2026-03-09 and open/rw-vicuna-13b@2026-03-09 as part of the same deployment.
- Observed across both SDK and direct REST streaming clients.

Steps to reproduce (customer flow):
1) Start a new chat session with a long system prompt (~600 tokens).
2) Send an initial user message that triggers a generation of ~150-300 tokens.
3) Observe the stream: client waits for first token for 300-800ms sometimes; subsequent tokens stream normally.

Observed behavior:
- Delayed first-token emission (TTFB spike).
- No reproducible request failure - majority still succeed after delay.
- Increased CPU on prefill workers and observed KV cache miss rates higher than baseline.

Expected behavior:
- First token within previous baseline (<=150ms p50) and stable streaming cadence.

Logs & traces:
- Traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/SUP-19321/trace-0001 (prefill path shows serialization stall)
- Metric snapshot (last 24h): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ttfb/greenfield-case
- Customer-side sample session: provided in attachment (chat_session_2026-03-09.json).

Temporary mitigation requested by customer:
- If possible, roll the pool back to runtime 2.1.4 and model bundle prior to the upgrade. Customer reported recovery after a targeted rollback on a single host.

Notes:
- Customer SLA flagged this as impacting product demos; support engaged SRE and runtime to triage.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maya Patel (Support): Opened ticket after receiving customer report and validated latency spikes in our dashboards. Added SRE oncall.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Jonah Kim (SRE): Correlated the start of increased KV cache miss rate with runtime 2.1.6 rollout. CPU on prefill pod tasks spiked during initial token generation window. Scheduling a targeted rollback of the dedicated pool as an immediate test.
2026-03-10 12:30 - Greenfield AI (Customer): Confirming that rolling back one host to previous runtime restored expected TTFB for test sessions. Asking for full-pool rollback or hotfix.

2026-03-11 02:20 - Runtime Team (Engineer: Priya Rao): We observed a change in kernel selection heuristics in 2.1.6 that increases setup time for certain quantized attention kernels on sequences with long system prompts. Creating PR to revert the heuristic while we analyze impact. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2874

2026-03-12 09:45 - Jonah Kim (SRE): Applied staged rollback to remaining hosts in greenfield-dedicated-1 and re-ran customer test cases; p50 first-token fell back to ~95ms. Continuing collection of traces for full postmortem.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection / compilation path in runtime 2.1.6 introduced extra setup time for certain model shapes and quantization combos.
2) KV cache warmup behavior changed causing more prefix recomputation and higher CPU during prefill.
3) Scheduling/backpressure at the streaming layer causing client-level buffering before first token.

What we checked:
- Checked runtime logs: increased 'kernel_compile' entries between 02:00-02:10 UTC on rollout hosts.
- Profiled prefill: CPU time per request rose by ~3x for affected requests; the spike correlates to long system prompts.
- Tracing shows the delay is between prefill completion and the first token send path (setup/serialize step).
- No increased 5xx errors or memory OOMs.

Partial findings:
- Reverting kernel selection heuristic in a dev branch removes the 300-600ms stall in instrumented runs.
- Rolling back runtime on one host returns expected TTFB in customer tests.

Next steps:
- Runtime team to merge hotfix revert (PR 2874) and cut 2.1.7 candidate.
- Plan: staged rollout of 2.1.7 to dedicated pools under canary monitoring focused on TTFB and kernel compile counts.
- Postmortem to capture root cause, release checklist updates to include TTFB metric sanity checks.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: staged rollback to runtime 2.1.4/previous model bundles in the affected dedicated pool reduced TTFB to baseline.
Action items: Runtime team to land PR that reverts the kernel-selection heuristic and publish 2.1.7. Add automated canary checks for first-token latency for future rollouts.
Status: Waiting on runtime PR merge and verified canary rollout; customer notified and monitoring continues.
workaround: Staged rollback of dedicated pool to runtime 2.1.4 and previous model bundles. Customers can pin to pre-upgrade model bundle as temporary workaround.
follow_up_tasks: Merge hotfix PR and cut 2.1.7 release
Add TTFB gating to rollout pipeline
